name: Old Malay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: No phonology or stress section; cites Teeuw 1959, Collins 1998, Sneddon 2003.

sources.citation: Griffiths, Arlo. 2020. The Old Malay Mañjuśrīgṛha inscription from Candi Sewu (Java, Indonesia). In Tournier, Eltschinger & Sernesi (eds), Archaeologies of the Written, 225-262. Naples: UniorPress. (HAL halshs-03013600)
sources.note: Edition, translation and linguistic commentary of one OM inscription; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Griffiths, Arlo. 2018. The Corpus of Inscriptions in the Old Malay Language. In Daniel Perret (ed.), Writing for Eternity: A Survey of Epigraphy in Southeast Asia, 275-283. Paris: EFEO. (HAL hal-01920769)
sources.note: Defines and inventories the OM inscriptional corpus (building on Mahdi 2005: 185); epigraphic, nothing on stress/phonology.

sources.citation: Adelaar, K. Alexander. 1992. Proto-Malayic: The reconstruction of its phonology and parts of its lexicon and morphology. Pacific Linguistics C-119. Canberra: ANU. 266 pp.
sources.note: Stress statements only for the modern isolects (SM p. 9: penultimate unless penult has schwa + single consonant, then final; non-phonemic; same pattern for Minangkabau, Banjar, Serawai, Iban). Old Malay is used as auxiliary evidence (p. 5; sec. 6.4 pp. 163ff. is morphological); nothing on OM or Proto-Malayic stress. p. 59 only reports Zorc's (1983) pre-PM 'accent pattern favouring the last syllable' as an explanation of SM c; p. 163 infers PM *mAr- 'was never stressed' because prefixed to disyllabic lexemes.

sources.citation: Adelaar, K. Alexander. 1992. The relevance of Salako for Proto-Malayic and for Old Malay epigraphy. BKI 148(3/4): 381-408. doi:10.1163/22134379-90003143
sources.note: Historical phonology and morphology bearing on OM epigraphy; no mention of stress or accent (only 'antepenultimate' vowels).

sources.citation: Teeuw, A. 1959. The history of the Malay language: A preliminary survey. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 115(2): 138-156.
sources.note: Discusses the phonology of the Old Malay inscriptions (four vowel phonemes a, pepet, i, u; mid vowels only in Sanskrit loans; pp. 140-146) but says nothing about stress or accent (grep 'stress|accent' = 0 hits).

sources.citation: Mahdi, Waruno. 2005. Old Malay. In K.A. Adelaar & N. Himmelmann (eds), The Austronesian Languages of Asia and Madagascar, 182-201. London/New York: Routledge.
